rounds.text: Jay Shree Tea & Industries Ltd trades at a substantial discount to its intrinsic asset value, with a price-to-book ratio of 0.62x on a book value of ₹ 132 against a share price of ₹ 81.6 [E1]. This asset protection is further highlighted by a key-ratios provider P/B of 0.53x, which sits dramatically below the sector benchmark of 1.79x [E6]. Operational momentum is showing early signs of acceleration rather than stagnation, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 8% [E16] and a year-over-year sales increase of 9% [E62]. Compounded sales growth has also ticked upward across medium-term horizons, showing 5% over 3 years [E15] compared to a 3% rate across 5 and 10 years [E13, E14]. Conceded: the company carries negative returns on assets at -3.01% [E7] and equity at -7.51% [E8], alongside a sharp drop in trailing profit growth of -174% [E19]. Despite these headwinds, the tiny ₹ 236 Cr market capitalisation [E2] offers an exceptionally low entry multiple for an asset-rich balance sheet positioned near the bottom quarter of its 52-week range [E4].

Conceded: the share price sits at ₹ 81.6 against a book value of ₹ 132 [E1], and the price-to-book ratio is 0.53x against a sector benchmark of 1.79x [E6]. However, the bull's reliance on asset protection ignores that these assets generate negative returns, with a return on assets of -3.01% versus a sector benchmark of 3.52% [E7] and a return on equity of -7.51% against a sector benchmark of 8.45% [E8]. While the bull highlights a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 8% [E16] and a year-over-year increase of 9% [E62], this top-line movement has collapsed earnings quality, evidenced by a catastrophic compounded profit growth of -174% over the trailing twelve months [E19]. Furthermore, the bull's cited 3-year sales growth of 5% [E15] sits on top of secular stagnation, mirroring a miserable 10-year compounded sales growth of 3% [E13] and a 5-year compounded sales growth of 3% [E14], which is explicitly flagged as poor sales growth over the past five years [E58]. The scanX signal engine confirms that earnings growth is decelerating [E64] and that recent price growth exceeds profit growth by 148% [E53], proving that expectations are running dangerously ahead of delivery rather than offering a rational margin of safety.
